req.title: Create schema on startup
req.statement: The system shall create the tasks table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-024 requires that the tasks table is created via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup. The primary observable effect is that the app is reachable (HTTP 200 on root) and the /tasks/ endpoint is functional (HTTP 200, returns a list) immediately after import — proving the table exists. We also verify the table is queryable by POSTing a task (positive EP), confirm the root payload fields exactly (mutation-resilient), test that a missing table would surface as 500 (negative/NEG via a fresh engine without create_all), and use BVA to confirm the empty-table boundary returns an empty list rather than an error.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_root_endpoint_returns_200_with_exact_payload():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["message"] == "Welcome to Task Manager API"
    assert body["version"] == "1.0.0"
    assert body["docs"] == "/docs"
    assert len(body) == 3

tests.name: test_startup_schema_allows_task_creation_and_retrieval
preconditions: tasks table created at startup via create_all
expected: Response contains id (int), title matching input, completed == false
GET returns HTTP 200 with same id and title
trace: R-TASK-024: table created at startup enables full CRUD state transition; POST then GET proves schema is live
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_schema_allows_task_creation_and_retrieval():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "startup test task", "description": "verify schema", "completed": False}
    r_post = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    created = r_post.json()
    assert isinstance(created["id"], int)
    assert created["title"] == "startup test task"
    assert created["description"] == "verify schema"
    assert created["completed"] == False
    assert "created_at" in created
    task_id = created["id"]
    r_get = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    fetched = r_get.json()
    assert fetched["id"] == task_id
    assert fetched["title"] == "startup test task"
    assert fetched["completed"] == False

test_startup_schema_allows_task_creation_and_retrieval()

tests.name: test_no_schema_causes_500_on_tasks_query
preconditions: A fresh in-memory SQLite engine is created WITHOUT calling create_all
A minimal FastAPI app is wired to that engine
actions: Build a FastAPI app that skips create_all
expected: HTTP 500 because the tasks table does not exist
Confirms that create_all at startup is the critical step
trace: R-TASK-024 negative path: omitting create_all causes server error, proving the requirement is necessary
tests.executable:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, Session
from typing import List
from app import models, schemas, crud

def test_no_schema_causes_500_on_tasks_query():
    bad_engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
    BadSession = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=bad_engine)
    # Intentionally skip: models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=bad_engine)
    bad_app = FastAPI()
    def get_bad_db():
        db = BadSession()
        try:
            yield db
        finally:
            db.close()
    @bad_app.get("/tasks/")
    def read_tasks_bad(db: Session = Depends(get_bad_db)):
        return crud.get_tasks(db=db)
    client = TestClient(bad_app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    r = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r.status_code == 500

test_no_schema_causes_500_on_tasks_query()

tests.name: test_startup_schema_tasks_table_name_and_columns_exist
actions: Inspect table names via SQLAlchemy inspection
Verify tasks table and key columns are present
expected: Columns id, title, description, completed, created_at, updated_at all present
trace: R-TASK-024: create_all must produce a table named 'tasks' with the exact columns defined in models.Task
tests.executable:
from sqlalchemy import inspect as sa_inspect
from app.database import engine
from app.main import app  # triggers create_all

def test_startup_schema_tasks_table_name_and_columns_exist():
    inspector = sa_inspect(engine)
    table_names = inspector.get_table_names()
    assert "tasks" in table_names
    columns = {col["name"] for col in inspector.get_columns("tasks")}
    assert "id" in columns
    assert "title" in columns
    assert "description" in columns
    assert "completed" in columns
    assert "created_at" in columns
    assert "updated_at" in columns
    assert len(columns) == 6

test_startup_schema_tasks_table_name_and_columns_exist()

tests.name: test_startup_tasks_endpoint_skip_zero_limit_one_boundary
actions: POST one task to ensure at least one row
expected: First GET returns exactly 1 item list
Second GET returns exactly empty list
trace: R-TASK-024 + BVA: schema exists and supports pagination boundary at limit=1 and skip=1
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_tasks_endpoint_skip_zero_limit_one_boundary():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r_post = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "bva task", "completed": False})
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    r1 = client.get("/tasks/?skip=0&limit=1")
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    body1 = r1.json()
    assert isinstance(body1, list)
    assert len(body1) == 1
    assert body1[0]["title"] == "bva task"
    r2 = client.get("/tasks/?skip=1&limit=1")
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert isinstance(body2, list)
    assert len(body2) == 0

test_startup_tasks_endpoint_skip_zero_limit_one_boundary()
